title: Golden Hour Scout dataset
description: One item per photography window, plus one explanatory item for any local day that has no windows. All 7 local days always appear.

date.title: Solar day
date.description: Local date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the solar day that produced this item — NOT a restatement of startLocal's date. Above roughly 60° latitude an evening window can end after local midnight, so endLocal may carry the next date while this does not. Read boundary dates from startLocal/endLocal, never from here.

type.title: Item type
type.description: One of the four photography windows, or one of the two explanatory shapes emitted for a local day with zero windows.

reason.title: No-window reason
reason.description: Present only on polar and noWindows items. "no-boundary-crossings" is an ordinary day, with a real sunrise and sunset, on which the sun still never reaches the golden/blue-hour elevation boundaries — deliberately not labelled polar, which would be factually wrong.

startLocal.title: Start
startLocal.description: Window start as ISO-8601 local time with an explicit numeric UTC offset — never bare UTC, never the runner's own zone. Absent on polar and noWindows items.

endLocal.title: End
endLocal.description: Window end as ISO-8601 local time with an explicit numeric UTC offset. May carry the next calendar date at high latitudes. Absent on polar and noWindows items.

condition.title: Condition
condition.description: WMO label of the hourly sample closest to the window's midpoint, ties going to the later hour, or "n/a" if that sample carried no weather code.

wmoCode.title: WMO code
wmoCode.description: Raw WMO weather code backing `condition`, or null if the forecast reported none for that hour.

conditionSequence.title: Condition sequence
conditionSequence.description: One condition label per hour overlapping [start, end), duplicates kept.

idealSky.title: Ideal sky
idealSky.description: True only on evidence: a dry, unobscured WMO code AND all four cloud figures inside their bands simultaneously. A figure the forecast omitted counts as unknown rather than 0%, so an incomplete forecast yields no ideal-sky windows instead of a verdict on partial data.

conditions.title: Cloud & precipitation
conditions.description: Figures from the hourly sample closest to the window's midpoint. Percent 0-100, or null where the forecast omitted that variable — which is not the same as 0.

cloudTotal.title: Total cloud cover %
cloudTotal.description: An independent whole-sky reading, not the sum or maximum of the three layer figures — layers overlap, so they routinely sum past 100%.

cloudLow.title: Low cloud %
cloudLow.description: Whole-sky low-cloud cover. Open-Meteo reports no bearing, so this cannot say whether the cloud sits on the sun-side horizon specifically.

sun.title: Sun
sun.description: Sunrise and sunset for the item's solar day, plus the sun's bearing mid-window. Absent on polar and noWindows items.

sunrise.title: Sunrise
sunrise.description: ISO-8601 local time with UTC offset, or null on a polar day/night where the event does not occur.

sunset.title: Sunset
sunset.description: ISO-8601 local time with UTC offset, or null on a polar day/night where the event does not occur.

azimuthAtPeak.title: Azimuth at midpoint
azimuthAtPeak.description: Compass azimuth in degrees, north-clockwise, at the window's temporal midpoint.

location.title: Location
location.description: The resolved place, repeated on every item. On the `coordinates` input path there is no place record, so `name` is the formatted lat/lon — a mistyped pair stays visible rather than being silently geocoded away.

name.title: Name
name.description: Composite display name: name[, admin1][, country], missing parts skipped.

admin1.title: State / province
admin1.description: Raw admin1 field from the geocoding API, when it supplied one.

country.title: Country
country.description: Raw country field from the geocoding API, when it supplied one.

timezone.title: IANA timezone
timezone.description: Resolved from geocoding, or from the forecast's timezone=auto read-back on the `coordinates` path. A missing zone fails the run; it is never defaulted to UTC or the runner's zone.
